Janusz Waluś

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Who is the man behind one of the Apartheid regime's most notorious murders?

Summary:
Born in Poland before immigrating to SA in 1981,Janusz Waluś became a citizen in 1987. He soon became involved in right wing politics, becoming a member of the Conservative Party as well as the AWB. On Easter sunday 1993, the name Waluś would forever be burnt into the national psyche when Janusz drove to MK chief of staff Chris Hani's house and shot and killed Hani.


Further information:
We have stock footage of: the murder scene, Hani making anti violence speeches, and related events of the time. We also have stock of widow Limpho Hani at some of the recent court appearances where Waluś has been cleared for parole and the court judgment saying he should be released in 14 days.The SACP have agreed to an interview with a high ranking member who knew Hani. Author Janet Smith who wrote Hani's biography has also agreed to an interview aswell as retired Brigadier Ivan Human who was the cop in charge of the Hani murder investigation. I am in contact with Witold Waluś, Janusz's brother, who has agreed to an off the record conversation about his brother as well as providing us with family photographs of Janusz. I've requested an on cam interview with Witold who has promised to get back to me today. He was originally reluctant, but after clearing any legal concerns with Janusz's lawyer Julian Knight I'm hoping Witold will agree to the interview. We are also going to speak to lawyer Micheal Motsoeneng to analyse the Justice Department's ongoing attempts to stop the parole process. If Witold does not agree to the interview we would have to use the info he gives us on Janusz as voice and the family pics as visuals to sketch a portrait of the man, and intercut that with our other interviews.

Press Release:


Who is Janusz Waluś?
Easter Sunday – 1993. Polish immigrant and right wing extremist Janusz Waluś drove to the home of MK chief of staff and political activist Chris Hani, and shot him in cold blood. After 23 years behind bars the High Court recently sanctioned Waluś exit from prison on parole, sparking outrage. Now with opposition to his release escalated to the Supreme Court of Appeal, Carte Blanche asks - who is the man behind one of apartheid’s most notorious murders?


Script:


Janusz Waluś
22 April 2016

On Screen Text & Music
As the Apartheid regime collapsed in the early 1990’s
The country was torn apart by civil unrest, violence and bloodshed
One event brought us closer to civil war than any other

Sound Up Nelson Mandela
The coldblooded murder of Chris Hani has sent shockwaves throughout the country and the world. Our grief and anger is tearing us apart.

Sound Up
Umkhonto we Siswe song

Voice
On the 10th of April 1993 Martin Thembisile Hani, later known as Chris Hani, then leader of the South African Communist Party and chief of staff of Umkhonto we Siswe, was shot to death outside his house in Dawn Park, Boksburg.

Link Derek
Chris Hani’s assassination came at an extremely volatile time in this country’s history. And it had a huge impact on the politics of that era.

Sound Up Nelson Mandela
A deed so foul, that our whole nation now teeters on the brink of disaster.

Sound Up Janet Smith
There was so much violence, particularly in this area, and so you know that kind of heightened political consciousness was driving fear.

Voice
Janet Smith is the executive editor of The Star newspaper and co-authored Chris Hani’s biography with Beauregard Tromp. She says Hani was a leader loved and respected by his people.

Sound Up Janet
Likeable, affable, a man who yes, in a clichéd way we would say of the people, but that is how he came across.

Sound Up Chris Hani
No Nuremburg trials in a future South Africa. We want reconciliation. This country has been bleeding for a long time.

Voice
Janusz Jacub Waluś, the man who shot and killed Chris Hani, was caught within minutes of the crime, after an eye witness phoned police and gave them the registration number of the vehicle Waluś was driving.

Sound Up Nelson Mandela
A white woman, of Afrikaner origin, risked her life, so that we may know, and bring to justice, this assassin.

Sound Up Ivan Human
Ivan: This patrol car with two members from Boksburg was standing at a stop street. And they stopped and saw this car in front of them. And the message had just come over with the registration number.

Derek: Which had one figure wrong?

Ivan: One figure ja, one figure was wrong, and immediately they acted and they pulled up and they apprehended him.

Voice
Retired Brigadier Ivan Human was the commander of the East Rand Murder and Robbery Unit at the time of Hani’s murder, and was in charge of the investigation. He says although Walus was arrested almost immediately, he was a tough nut to crack.

Sound Up Ivan
Ivan: I put up different teams, and they interrogated, for say two hours, and then replaced by the next fresh team and the next fresh team. And then we carried on like that. But there was never a breakdown.

Derek: He never cracked?

Ivan: Never cracked.

Link Derek
Much has been reported in all the media over the years, but who is the man behind the assassination of Chris Hani. This man who immigrated to South Africa from Poland way back in 1981.

Voice
Born in 1953 in Zakopane, Poland, Janusz Walus was the youngest son of Dadeusz and Teresa Walus. At the time Poland was a satellite state of the brutal communist regime of the USSR.


Sound Up Janet
And of course the irony is that his family left Poland out of fear of the communists, living under a system they couldn’t abide. And yet he came here, with a system that was intolerable and detested around the world for it’s racism, and that seemed to be acceptable to his family.

Sound Up Ivan
I’ve never seen a guy that operated like that, he just doesn’t talk. I think he’s probably born and bred like that.

Voice
The fiercely anti communist Janusz enjoyed sports, achieving a black belt in Karate and winning various motor sport titles in Poland. Before coming to South Africa he met and married wife Wanda, and they had a daughter together named Ewa.

Sound Up Janet
The Apartheid government was giving very favorable loans to immigrants at that time. And they had a glass cutting business and they lived in quite an affluent area.

Voice
Janusz became a member of the Conservative Party and was attracted to right wing politics. At some point during the 80’s he met Clive Derby Lewis and his wife Gaye.

Sound Up Janet
And Derby-Lewis, who occupied quite an important position in South African society; he was a member of the president’s council, he was a member of parliament, was more driven by what the conservative party could do if the country fell apart, could they sieze the political impetus back that they had had in the late 80’s. And then you had Walus who was kind of on the fringes, probably as a relatively willing tool.

Voice
Back in ’93 police soon connected Walus to Derby Lewis. A week after Chris Hani’s murder Ivan arrived at Clive’s house with an arrest warrant in his hand.

Sound Up Ivan
I took out the warrant, and as I said to Clive, I said are you Mr. Clive Derby-Lewis? I said I’m arresting you now on a charge of murder. And Clive got such a shock that he fell, and I grabbed him as he went down, and I laid him down on the sofa there.

Voice
Janusz Walus, Clive and Gaye Derby-Lewis stood trial for the murder of Chris Hani in October ‘93. Gaye was acquitted of all charges, but both Janusz and Clive were found guilty and sentenced to death. Later on their sentences were commuted to life in prison.

Sound Up Janet
Derek: Janet what’s your opinion on the legal ramifications around the possibility of his parole?
Janet: It’s such an emotional issue, probably the most emotional legal matter that post democratic South Africa has ever faced really.

Voice
Last year Clive Derby-Lewis was granted medical parole, but Justice Minister Michael Masutha denied Walus’s parole bid. Walus’ legal council then took the matter to the North Gauteng High Court, and Judge Nicolene Janse van Niewenhuizen gave her judgment in March this year.

Link Derek
On the 10th of March the North Gauteng High Court ordered that Janusz Walus, the man who assassinated SACP leader Chris Hani be released on parole within 14 days.

Voice
The decision sparked outrage amongst SACP members and also Limpho Hani, Chris Hani’s widow.

Sound Up Solly Mapaila
Parole is not a constitutional right, it is a privilege that is granted to prisoners who are incarcerated after they’ve met particular requirements, and it’s looked at on the basis of individual merit of each prisoner.

Link Derek
Last week Judge Janse van Niewenhuizen dismissed the justice minister’s application for leave to appeal her earlier judgment, prompting the minister and the SACP to take matters further.

Sound Up Judge Nicolene janse van Niewenhuizen
In this matter I’ve prepared a written judgment of which I only read the order. The first respondent’s application for leave to appeal is dismissed, two: the first respondent is ordered to pay the costs of the application, which costs include the costs of two council.

Voice
Constitutional law expert Pierre de Vos believes the Justice Minister might have been right in denying parole to Walus, since the murder was politically motivated and could have had a devastating effect on the country.

Sound Up Pierre
So this makes it different from some of the other cases that the minister might have considered in which the minister did grant parole, because this was clearly a crime that was really trying to stop South Africa from becoming a democracy.

Voice
Limpho Hani expressed her concerns about the decision after court.

Sound Up Limpho
The fact that this particular judge decides to deny the minister to appeal, it says to me she is not very sure of the decision that she took and she seems to be afraid for another court to look at this.

Voice
Solly Mapaila is the second deputy general secretary of the SACP. He says Walus should not be granted parole because he’s never told the whole story behind the assasination.

Sound Up Solly
Both the SACP and the Hani family have continued to oppose even the possibility for these murderers to be granted parole on the basis of not disclosing the whole truth.

Sound Up Pierre de Vos
The fact of the matter is that the law that is applicable to Mr. Walus does not gove Mr. Walus the automatic right to be given parole after the requisite twenty year period. It says that the minister still has the final say.

Voice
The ongoing legal battle begs the question, are we all equal under the law or was this a crime like no other?

Sound Up Pierre
although people could differ about whether the high court erred or didn’t err, I think that there is at least the possibility that the Supreme Court of Appeal or the Constitutional Court will come to a different decision than the high court, so I don’t think personally that it is an abuse of the minister’s powers or an abuse of the process to at least see what another court would say in this particular case.












Janus Walus
Promos script
23 April 2016

Promo 1
Voice
On Easter Sunday 1993 Polish immigrant Janusz Walus shot Mk Chief of Staff and SACP leader Chris Hani in cold blood.

Sound Up Singing

Voice
Who is the man behind one of Apartheid’s most notorious murders?

Promo 2
Voice Over
After 23 years behind bars the High Court recently sanctioned the parole of Apartheid assassin Janusz Walus, sparking a huge legal battle.

Sound Up SACP
Parole is not a constitutional right, it is a privilege.


Promo 10 sec
Voice
We analyse the legal battle between the minister of justice and Janusz Walus, and take a closer look at the murder which nearly brought a country to it’s knees.
